dct_description_sm: In the Mackenzie Valley Region, there is a north-south climatic gradient that is evident in the vegetation zonation and permafrost regimes.  The Mackenzie Valley also lies within a region that has been warming over the last 30 years and is predicted to be strongly impacted by future climate warming.  This project was designed to establish a series of scientifically sound monitoring sites which will allow us to quantify and monitor any effects of changing climate on the local vegetation and permafrost conditions.  It will be particularly relevant to understand the baseline environmental conditions in the face of the proposed pipeline which may introduce another disturbance factor, on top of climate change, to vegetation throughout the valley.  This project is being conducted in cooperation with the GNWT as it aids in baseline data collection fundamental to forest management in the NWT.  Methods and data collected will be made available to be used by any interested parties, including GNWT forest management, the MVP panel, as well as the scientific and local communities.  Because transitional regions are particularly sensitive to changes, we are particularly interested in peat plateaux where permafrost is already showing evidence of collapse.  Plots are located in peat plateaux, collapse scars, and adjacent upland forests, with a series of detailed, contiguous 1 x 1 m plots on the collapse scar margin, to  detect any permafrost/vegetation changes on a smaller scale.
